member.name: T:MediaDevices.OpCodes
member.summary: Base operation codes (opcodes) used in Picture Transfer Protocol (PTP) and vendor-specific device communication.

remarks.para: This enum holds the manufacturer-independent opcodes. Vendor-specific opcodes are in the OpCodesCanon, OpCodesNikon, OpCodesSony, OpCodesPanasonic, OpCodesSamsung, OpCodesLeica and OpCodesFujifilm enums.

The enum is organized into the following categories:
PTP Commands (0x1001 - 0x101C): Standard Picture Transfer Protocol commands for basic device operations.
MTP Extensions (0x9201 - 0x9203): Standard MTP operations.
Vendor (0x9xxx): Generic vendor codes for unspecified manufacturers.
Microsoft Extensions (0x98xx): MTP (Media Transfer Protocol) extensions for object properties and references.

Each opcode is a 16-bit unsigned integer (ushort) that identifies a specific command to send to the device. Opcode values are only unique within one manufacturer - the same value can mean different commands for different vendors, which is why the vendor-specific opcodes use separate enums.

member.summary: Resolves the logical parent used for path construction.
member.remarks:
Most MTP devices expose a normal hierarchical object graph where each object has a WPD_OBJECT_PARENT_ID. Android devices usually behave like this.
Some devices, especially Apple devices exposing DCF-style storage, may not expose a usable ParentId for top-level folders. In those cases the object may instead expose WPD_OBJECT_CONTAINER_FUNCTIONAL_OBJECT_ID, which points to the closest functional object, typically the storage root.
This method keeps both behaviours in one place: 1. Use ParentId for normal hierarchical devices. 2. Treat functional storage objects as direct children of DEVICE. 3. Fall back to ParentContainerId for non-hierarchical / DCF-like devices.

This wrapper takes a defensive approach for device streams (MTP/WPD), where COM implementations are often incomplete or inconsistent:
